papers.title: A new efficient and accurate approximation for the dielectric function of the weakly coupled electron gas
papers.abstract: An accurate analytic approximation is developed for the real boundary component of a regularised, causal complex auxiliary function describing the random phase approximation dielectric response of the weakly coupled electron gas across classical to strongly degenerate conditions. Its collisionless imaginary boundary component is known exactly from the Fermi--Dirac occupation logarithm. Following an assessment of existing approximations and the establishment of a high-precision numerical benchmark, a two-regime representation is constructed: a $6/7$ rational function at weak and moderate degeneracy and a composite polynomial approximation at strong degeneracy. Exact asymptotic constraints determine the rational denominator algebraically, leaving six independent state functions. Branch-locked optimisation, Chebyshev parametrisation and Bernstein-basis constraints provide accurate, smooth and numerically pole-free behaviour. In the strongly degenerate regime, the logarithmic Kohn contribution is isolated explicitly, with its regular remainder represented by analytically integrable polynomial expansions. The approximation achieves a maximum relative error of approximately $0.11\%$ in the real dielectric integral across the investigated domain, accurately reproduces its scaled derivative and is substantially faster than numerical quadrature. Validation using the electron--electron dynamic structure factor and imaginary-time correlation function yields maximum plasmon peak-amplitude errors of approximately $1.04\%$ and maximum pointwise correlation-function errors below $0.166\%$. Comparisons with established approximations demonstrate substantial improvements, particularly for weakly damped collective excitations. The resulting model provides an accurate, computationally efficient foundation for electronic screening, dynamic dielectric calculations and X-ray Thomson scattering analysis.

papers.title: How zonal states beat-driven by Alfven eigenmodes stabilize micro-turbulence in tokamak plasmas
papers.abstract: The effects of zonal states (ZS) beat-driven by Alfven eigenmodes (AEs) on micro-turbulence stability are investigated; taking toroidal Alfven eigenmode (TAE) and ion temperature gradient mode (ITG) as an example. The analysis is carried out by deriving the nonlinear gyrokinetic equation describing particle response to ITG, in the presence of TAE beat-driven ZS. It is found that, the phase space zonal structure generated by AEs could lead to a significant reduction in the local nonuniformity drive and, thereby, stabilize the local ITG instabilities. The zonal flow induced shearing, on the other hand, contributes only to a real frequency shift and, typically, negligibly small additional stabilization.

papers.title: Energy transfers in decaying three-dimensional Hall-magnetohydrodynamics turbulence: Dependence on the Ion-Inertial Length and the Magnetic Prandtl Number
papers.abstract: We present a systematic study of energy transfers in three-dimensional (3D) decaying Hall-magnetohydrodynamics (HMHD) turbulence. Our study has been designed to investigate the dependence of these transfers on initial energy spectra, the ion-inertial length $d_{i}$, and the magnetic Prandtl number $Pr_{m}$. Using shell-to-shell decomposition, we compute the energy transfer rates for (a) kinetic-to-kinetic, (b) magnetic-to-magnetic, (c) kinetic-to-magnetic, and (d) magnetic-to-kinetic interactions by carrying out extensive pseudospectral direct numerical simulations (DNSs) of 3D HMHD and its MHD counterpart. Furthermore, we examine the magnetic-to-magnetic and current-density-to-magnetic energy transfers arising from the Hall term in this framework. Energy transfers between like fields -- namely, kinetic-to-kinetic and magnetic-to-magnetic -- are predominantly local and forward in direction, cascading energy from large to small length scales. This behavior is consistent with a self-similar flow structure in the inertial range. Cross-field transfers, between kinetic and magnetic energy, are found to be forward but non-local in character. At low and high $Pr_{m}$, the transfers become local, and the nonlinear energy transfer is significantly suppressed. Moreover, we observe that the Hall term drives both inverse and forward transfers of magnetic energy, associated with local and non-local transfer, respectively.

papers.title: Dephasing-free plasma acceleration with millijoule picosecond lasers
papers.abstract: Laser-plasma accelerators reach gradients a thousand times above radio-frequency cavities, but need joule-class femtosecond lasers firing about once per second, and electrons outrun the wave. A comb of laser lines spaced by the plasma frequency, each in its own mode of a matched channel, drives a wake moving at the speed of light. In particle-in-cell simulations a 175\,mJ, 0.5\,ps drive holds 21\,GV/m over 10\,mm with a 0.15\,rad phase drift; a test electron gains 208\,MeV, 2.6 times more than in one mode. Because the wave builds up resonantly, the required energy falls steeply with density: a 29\,mJ drive sustains 20\,GV/m, and a 10\,mJ drive, within reach of kilohertz industrial lasers, gives a test electron 170\,MeV over 30\,mm. A simulated stage transfers 5\,\% of the laser energy to the wake; the Manley--Rowe limit is about 18\,\% for five lines.

papers.title: Aggregating soft-photon recoil with a positive finite-step sampler
papers.abstract: We model stochastic radiation reaction by aggregating soft photons into one positive recoil, retaining the local no-emission probability and two loss moments of the crossed-field QED kernel. Unlike Gaussian diffusion, the sampler preserves one-sided energy loss. Analytical synchrotron moments expose a finite-step cooling bias, which state feedback reduces. Laser and ion-channel tests probe excessive-loss risk and directed radiation spectra, providing a practical route to stochastic particle simulations without resolving individual soft emissions.

papers.title: Direct measurement of the on-shot focal-spot size of a kilojoule-class petawatt laser
papers.abstract: We report a direct, on-shot determination of the focal-spot size of a kilojoule-class, four-beam petawatt laser. Encircled-energy curves were inferred from the energy transmitted around aluminum-coated spheres of varying diameters placed at the focal plane. The 50% encircled-energy diameter D50 of each beam was obtained by fitting a two-component Gaussian mixture with Bayesian inference. With all deformable mirrors optimized in closed loop, the best-corrected alignment beam reached D50 = 34 (+4/-5) um, three times the diffraction limit of 10 um. Under full-power conditions, the thermal distortion of the main amplifier broadened this beam to D50 = 102 (+9/-8) um and reduced its peak intensity ninefold, to 2.2 (+0.6/-0.9) x 10^18 W/cm^2 at 250 J and 1.3 ps. The energy fraction of the narrow component decreased from 68% to 38%. These reference values serve facility users, and a deformable mirror upstream of the pulse compressor, now on one beam only, doubles the on-shot peak intensity.

papers.title: Nonlinearly Causal General-Relativistic Superfluid Hydrodynamics: Simulating Vortex Dynamics in Neutron-Star Interiors
papers.abstract: Neutron stars provide a natural laboratory for superfluid matter under extreme conditions. Its nonlinear dynamics is central to pulsar glitches, their possible links to fast radio bursts, and tidal interactions in inspiralling binaries. We develop a general-relativistic superfluid hydrodynamics framework incorporating entrainment, vortex forces, and line energy, and derive, for the first time, necessary and sufficient conditions for nonlinear causality and strong hyperbolicity. We also show that commonly used dissipative, force-balanced formulations without line tension are generically ill-posed at short wavelengths because of the Donnelly-Glaberson instability. Exploiting the analogy between vortex arrays with tension and force-free electrodynamics, we recast vortex dynamics in terms of effective electric and magnetic fields and drift velocities. This motivates a new finite-volume scheme combining constrained transport of superfluid vorticity with implicit electric-field evolution, enabling stable numerical evolution of the full system. We validate the scheme using an exact solution to the relativistic superfluid Riemann problem and Kelvin-wave dispersion relations, among other tests. Finally, we simulate dynamical, global general-relativistic two-fluid neutron-star equilibria, validate their oscillation modes, and present the first simplified calculation of superfluid interior spin-down with prescribed vortex release and repinning. The resulting stationary state retains both a net twist in the vortex array and residual differential rotation of the superfluid. Our framework thus enables nonlinear numerical studies of general-relativistic superfluid dynamics in neutron-star interiors.
